neighbours.label: a wh-word opening a rhetorical question in the middle of a sentence (after all, what can you do; who knew; how about we)
fire: The money is already gone, so what difference does one more bill make?
She never calls anyway, and honestly, what good would an apology do now?
He missed the bus again — who could have guessed that?
It is only a small scratch, after all, what harm can it do?
The forecast says rain all week; why bother washing the car?
Everyone else got a pay rise, so how about we ask for one too?
The shop is closed on Sundays — what else is new?
If even the experts disagree, who are we to judge?
quiet: The money is already gone, so we checked what the bank had charged us.
She never calls anyway, and nobody knows what she does all day.
He missed the bus again and asked who could drive him in.
It is only a small scratch, but the vet explained what to watch for.
The forecast says rain all week, which is why the car stays dirty.
Everyone else got a pay rise, and we wondered how they managed it.
The shop is closed on Sundays, and the sign says what hours apply.
If even the experts disagree, we should ask who funded the study.

notes: card: ' what' x8, ' What' x4, ' How' x4, ' Why'/' why'; all rhetorical questions after a comma or dash. The + pole is the Chinese full-width comma. Near misses use the same wh-words in ordinary embedded clauses.
